To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HIV and HTLV-1 have evolved mechanisms to evade detection by CD8+ cytotoxic T- lymphocytes (CTLs); (2) the viral proteins that target the MHC class I pathway are the HIV-1 Nef and Vpu proteins and the HTLV-1 Tax and Rex proteins; (3) HIV and HTLv-1 target the MHC I pathway at different points; (4) the mechanisms of HIV and HTLV are different and distinct,
the HTLV-1 Tax and the HIV-1 nef proteins have evolved to target the same host proteins that are involved in the presentation of viral antigens to CD8+ T-cells.
the HTLV-1 Tax protein and the HIV-1 Nef and Vpu proteins are able to inhibit the presentation of antigenic peptides on the surface of the target cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the viral proteins in the immune evasion of HTLV-1 infected cells.
how HTLV-1, HIV-1 and other retroviral proteins evade the immune system and how these proteins can be targeted by the immune system to be recognized as foreign.
the mechanisms by which HTLV-1, HIV-1 and other viruses interfere with the immune response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HTLV-1 encodes a protein that blocks MHC-I presentation to CD8 T-cells and a protein that inhibits the function of the CD8 T-cel.
both HTLV-1 Tax and HIV-1 Tat proteins have the ability to inhibit MHC class I expression and/or presentation, which is a major mechanism of their evasion of CTLs.
the HTLV-1 Tax protein and HIV-1 Nef protein are the only viral proteins that have been shown to be involved with the down-regulation of the major histocompatibilty complex (MHC) class I molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the retroviral proteins that block the major histocompatability complex (MHC) class I antigen presentation pathway are the most effective viral immune evasion strategies known to date.

the viral proteins that are responsible for evading MHC class I-mediated immune responses are encoded by the same gene, but have diverged to the point that the proteins encoded by these genes are not homologous.
both HTLV-1, and HIV-1 encode proteins that target MHC class I molecules, and that these proteins are important for immune evasion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retroviral proteins U and Vpu, respectively, of HTLV-1 (U) and HIV-1 (Vpu), target the major histocmpatibility complex class I (MHC class I) pathway to avoid detection by the immune system.
HTLV-1 has evolved a more complex mechanism to evade CTLs than HIV-1.
both HTLV-1 Tax and HIV-1 Nef proteins are able to target the major histcompatibility complex class I pathway, and that the mechanism(s) of action are different.
